title: Locally ringed topoi and local geometric morphisms
statement: Work with small sites in [def-weil-size-convention]. For a sheaf of rings $R$ on a site $\mathcal C$, let $|R|$ denote its underlying sheaf of sets and $R^\times$ its sheaf of units, with the inclusion $\iota_R:R^\times\to |R|$. The ringed topos $(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),R)$ is locally ringed if (i) for every object $U$ and section $a\in R(U)$ there is a covering sieve $V$ on $U$ such that, for every $f:W\to U$ in $V$, either $R(f)(a)$ or $1-R(f)(a)$ is invertible in $R(W)$; and (ii) if $0=1$ in $R(U)$, the empty sieve covers $U$. Equivalently in (ii), the equalizer of the zero and one maps to $|R|$ is the initial sheaf. A ringed-topos morphism $g:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),R)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),S)$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] is local if there exists a map $v:g^{-1}(S^\times)\to R^\times$ such that the square with upper arrow $v$, left arrow $g^{-1}(\iota_S)$, right arrow $\iota_R$, and lower arrow $g^\sharp:g^{-1}|S|\to |R|$ is cartesian. When both topoi are locally ringed, these are their local morphisms.
